subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB344.md LANDED. GR6 - the declarative runs on unsuccessful execution 'unless an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase takes precedence', scoped by b)-e) to the open mode, 'for any file open in the input mode or in the process of being opened in the input mode' and its three siblings (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 PASS on both fragments). Both halves of the PARTIAL are closed. (1) THE TIER PAIR IS WRITTEN ONCE. The GR3 a)/GR5 file-name switch and the GR3 b)/GR6 b)-e) open-mode switch were rendered in THREE places, not the two the note found: DispatchEmitter.__IoCheck, EcEmitter.__IoCheckEc and ProgramEmitter.__RunGlobalUse (the GR4 b) outward GLOBAL walk). All three now render through the one CodeGen/UseTierEmitter, so a fourth selector cannot drift from the rule. (2) THE EDITION QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS 'INVARIANT'. Annex E.2 item 19 a)/b) records that the previous standards did not run the open-mode tier for an unphrased invalid key, nor for a READ exception that is neither invalid key nor at end. Implemented as a <=2014 guard, that made FIVE NIST CCVS programs RED on CI - SQ122A, SQ136A, SQ137A, SQ138A (a '46' READ after at end, requiring USE AFTER EXCEPTION PROCEDURE INPUT to run) and SQ148A (a '47' READ on a file open OUTPUT, requiring the OUTPUT declarative), SQ137A failing with the literal remark 'INPUT DECLARATIVE NOT EXECUTED' against ANSI X3.23-1985 VII-2 1.3.5, VII-51 4.6.4(5). The guard was WITHDRAWN on the standard's own terms: Annex E is informative, E.1 scopes it to ONE prior edition (the 2014 one), and item 19's justification classes the prior state as defective TEXT - 'not clear or missing processing of some I-O exceptions' - which is a silence, not a prohibition. Note also that item 19 b) names only 'any declarative that specifies INPUT or I-O', so SQ148A's OUTPUT declarative was never in its scope: the guard was over-broad on its own terms as well. (3) THE TESTS. pb344_use_mode_read_exception ships at all four editions with IDENTICAL expected output - that identity IS the assertion: R1 ('47' on a READ against an OUTPUT-mode file), R2 (the at end family), R3 ('46') and R4 (a FAILED OPEN, holding GR6 b)'s 'in the process of being opened' half) all reach the mode tier at every edition. pb344_use_mode_invalid_key covers the GR5 file-name-before-mode precedence and the phrase-takes-precedence clause. pb344_use_f3_perform_preempt closes the leading exception-checking-PERFORM clause that had no test at all: Q1's matching WHEN preempts and IGNORES the declarative (GR17) and Q2's non-matching one falls to the USE tiers.
